Logging

1. Default Logging
  • Ignite uses java.util.logging (JUL) by default;
  • Log files are stored in $IGNITE_HOME/work/log/;
  • Start in verbose mode with ignite.sh -v or set IGNITE_QUIET=false;
2. Supported Logging Frameworks
FrameworkModule
java.util.logging (JUL)Built-in (default)
Log4j2ignite-log4j2
SLF4Jignite-slf4j
Jakarta Commons Logging (JCL)ignite-jcl
3. Using Log4j2
  • Add the module: 
    <dependency>
    <groupId>org.apache.ignite</groupId>
    <artifactId>ignite-log4j2</artifactId>
    <version>2.17.0</version>
</dependency>
  • Configure: 
    IgniteConfiguration cfg = new IgniteConfiguration();
cfg.setGridLogger(new Log4J2Logger("log4j2.xml"));
4. Using SLF4J
  • Add the module: 
    <dependency>
    <groupId>org.apache.ignite</groupId>
    <artifactId>ignite-slf4j</artifactId>
    <version>2.17.0</version>
</dependency>
  • Ignite automatically detects SLF4J on the classpath and uses it;
  • Pair with Logback, Log4j2-SLF4J bridge, or any SLF4J implementation;
5. Logging Best Practices
  • Use INFO level in production; switch to DEBUG only when troubleshooting;
  • Don't store logs in /tmp — it is cleared on server restart;
  • Archive old logs periodically;
  • Ensure sufficient disk space for log storage;
  • Monitor for ERROR and WARN level messages — they often indicate configuration issues or resource exhaustion;
